title: The Odyssey — the Regulars' Cut, played by hand

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The gods take their places in a widening ring. Poseidon’s seat remains empty.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Father Zeus, let Aegisthus lie in the ruin he earned. It is Odysseus my heart breaks for, wise, unlucky Odysseus, held against his will on Calypso's island, longing only for the sight of smoke rising from his own hearth. Has he not paid you sacrifice enough on the plain of Troy, Olympian?

segs.speaker: Zeus
segs.caption: My child, how could I forget godlike Odysseus? It is Poseidon the earth-shaker who rages without rest for the blinding of his Cyclops son, and drives that man from his homecoming. But come, let us here shape his return; one god cannot hold out against us all.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Then send Hermes, the guide, the slayer of Argus, across the water to Ogygia at once. Let him stand before the nymph Calypso with our fixed decree: hard-enduring Odysseus goes home.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: And I go to Ithaca myself, to breathe strength into his son. I will set Telemachus on his feet, send him to call the Achaeans to assembly, and then across the sea to Pylos and Sparta for news of his father, so the boy may win a name among men.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena fastens the gold sandals, closes her hand around the spear, and drops from Olympus.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Wearing the shape of Mentes, Athena waits at the palace threshold with her spear upright.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Dice strike the floor; cups are filled; the suitors never look toward the gate.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus sees the unattended stranger and crosses the hall, ashamed of his own house.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Welcome, stranger. You are kindly come to our house; give me your spear. Eat first, and afterward tell me what you need, but come, away from this noise.

items.title: Athena Arms Telemachus with a Course

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Now hear me, and do it. Tomorrow call the Achaean lords to assembly and bid the suitors scatter, each man to his own home. Then fit out a ship of twenty oars and go for news of your long-gone father, to Nestor at Pylos first, then to sandy Sparta and red-haired Menelaus, the last of the bronze-clad Achaeans home.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Have you not heard what fame Orestes won among men, striking down the schemer who murdered his famous father? You are tall and well-made, my friend; be brave, so that men born after you will speak your name. Childish things are done now; put them from you.

touch.text: Take the stranger's spear: pinch it

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Heralds, sound the call. Summon the long-haired Achaeans to assembly at first light, every man of them.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: He enters with two hounds and takes the seat that belonged to his father.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Old sir, that man is not far to seek: I called you, and the trouble is mine. I have lost my noble father, who was king among you here and gentle as a father; and now a greater ruin besides, suitors who beset my mother against her will and devour my house day after day. By Olympian Zeus and by Themis who seats the councils of men, I call it wrong, and I cannot fight it alone.

segs.speaker: Antinous
segs.caption: Bold-tongued Telemachus, do not lay your blame at our door. It is not the suitors who are at fault but your own mother, that queen of cunning; three years now, and nearly four, she has cheated the hearts of the Achaeans.

segs.speaker: Antinous
segs.caption: She set up her great loom in the hall, a shroud, she told us, for the lord Laertes, so no woman of the land could reproach her if he lay in death without a winding-sheet. All day she wove at that web, and every night, with torches set beside her, she unraveled it thread by thread.

segs.speaker: Antinous
segs.caption: Send her back to her father Icarius, and let her marry the man he names, and the man she chooses.

touch.text: Unweave the shroud: sweep your hand left and right

items.text: Two eagles tear the air over the assembly; the suitors laugh at the omen; by night the son takes wine and barley from the stores.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena, disguised as Telemachus, recruits crewmen and borrows Noemon's ship.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Telemachus, come out. Your companions sit at the oars already, waiting on your word; let us not delay the voyage.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The crew carries provisions from the palace and stows them below deck.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus boards.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena takes the pilot's seat and sends a strong west wind.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The sail fills, libations are poured, and the ship travels through the night.

items.text: Dawn at Pylos: black bulls on the beach for Poseidon.

segs.speaker: Nestor
segs.caption: Friend, you bring it all back, what we suffered on that plain, and the best of us fallen: Ajax lies there, and Achilles, and Patroclus wise as the gods, and my own strong Antilochus. And in every craft of war your father had no rival; no man alive could match Odysseus for cunning. Truly you are his son, your very speech is his.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Nestor begins the account of the quarrel that split the returning Greek fleet.

touch.text: Pour the libation: pinch the cup and tip it down

items.text: The war and the broken homecomings, drawn as the map Nestor speaks from.

segs.speaker: Nestor
segs.caption: Dear boy, no fear that you prove base or weak, when gods walk beside you so young, and that was no other of the Olympians but the daughter of Zeus himself, the glorious grey-eyed one who honored your father among the Argives. Be gracious, mistress: grant fair fame to me, to my children, to my honored wife, and I will sacrifice to you a yearling heifer, broad-browed, unbroken, her horns wrapped in gold.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus is bathed and dressed for departure.

items.text: The chariot road from Pylos to Sparta: two days of dust, and a double wedding in the halls of Menelaus.

books.title: The King and Queen of Sparta

segs.speaker: Helen
segs.caption: Menelaus, shall I speak what my eyes tell me? Never have I seen such likeness in man or woman — this must be Telemachus, the son Odysseus left a baby at home when for my shameless sake the Achaeans sailed to Troy.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Pisistratus confirms the identity and recalls his own dead brother Antilochus.

segs.speaker: Menelaus
segs.caption: Enough — we shame the feast with weeping. Let us remember supper now; with dawn there will be time for all our tales, and tears enough to go with them.

items.title: Helen's Drug and the Beggar in Troy

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Helen mixes a drug into the wine that quiets grief and anger.

segs.speaker: Helen
segs.caption: Hear one deed of that man of endurance. He scarred his own flesh with blows, threw a beggar's rags across his back, and walked through the gates of Troy — into the city of his enemies, looking like a slave.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Helen alone recognized and bathed him.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: he revealed the Greek plan after binding her to secrecy.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus killed Trojans and returned to the ships with intelligence.

segs.speaker: Menelaus
segs.caption: True, wife — yet you tell only half. Hear the horse's tale from within: I crouched in that timber belly with the best of the Argives, and Odysseus held command of us all, when you came circling in the dark.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Helen circled the horse and imitated the voices of the warriors' wives.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The hidden Greeks nearly answered.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus restrained them and silenced Anticlus.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus hears proof of his father's endurance and command under pressure.

touch.text: Helen circles the horse: trace a circle

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Menelaus and three men hid beneath sealskins and grappled the Old Man of the Sea.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Proteus changed into beasts, water, and a tree before yielding prophecy.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Proteus revealed that Odysseus lived, detained by Calypso on an island.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: When Telemachus will return your ship?

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Antinous selects a crew and sails to the strait between Ithaca and Same to ambush the prince.

segs.speaker: Medon
segs.caption: Queen, forgive the word I carry: the suitors plot to cut Telemachus down at sea as he sails home. I heard them lay the ambush with my own ears.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: she collapses in fear.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena sends a phantom in the shape of Iphthime to reassure the sleeping queen.

segs.speaker: Zeus
segs.caption: Hermes, my son, our messenger as always — go to the nymph of the braided hair and speak my fixed decree: Odysseus goes home. No god beside him, no mortal ship — on a lashed raft he shall come, through hardship, to Scheria on the twentieth day.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Hermes straps on his sandals, takes his wand, and skims across the sea.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Hermes reaches Ogygia, enters Calypso's fragrant cavern, and finds her weaving at the fire.

segs.speaker: Calypso
segs.caption: Unhappy man, weep here no longer — I am ready now to let you go. Rise; cut long timbers and build yourself a broad raft, and I will stock her with bread and water and red wine, and send a fair wind behind you for home.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Calypso suspects a trap and demands a binding oath that she will not plan his ruin.

segs.speaker: Calypso
segs.caption: Then witness Earth, and the wide Heaven above, and the down-dripping water of Styx — the greatest oath the blessed gods can swear: I plot no ruin against you. I counsel you only as I would counsel my own heart.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Immortality with her surpasses Penelope.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Goddess and queen, do not be angry — I know it all: wise Penelope must fade beside you, for she is mortal and you are deathless. Even so, every day I long for home and the hour of my return. And if some god wrecks me again on the wine-dark water, I will endure that too — my heart is old in suffering.

segs.speaker: Calypso
segs.caption: Here at the island's edge the tall trees stand — alder and poplar and sky-high fir, long dry, that will ride light on the water. Take the great bronze axe and the adze; here is cloth for a sail and cord to lace her. Build, and I will bring all the rest.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Calypso fells, trims, bores, joins, decks, and fences the timbers over four days.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Calypso rigs mast, yard, sail, steering oar, and ballast.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Calypso bathes and clothes him, loads food and water, and sends a warm wind behind the raft.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: For seventeen days Odysseus steers by the stars until Scheria rises ahead.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Poseidon sees him, gathers clouds, and strikes the sea with a four-wind storm.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The raft rolls.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus is swept away and barely regains it.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Abandon the raft and swim.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena restrains the winds except the north wind that drives him shoreward.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus swims for two nights and days while waves hurl him toward a reef-lined coast.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena shows him a river mouth free of rocks and wind.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Hear me, lord of this stream, whoever you are — I come to your current a suppliant, fleeing Poseidon's anger out of the sea. Even the deathless gods respect a wandering man who comes in need; pity me, lord, for I claim that mercy now.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus returns Ino's veil to the sea, crawls ashore, and hides beneath two intertwined olive bushes.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus buries himself in leaves and Athena seals him in sleep.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena reaches the palace of Alcinous and enters Nausicaa's chamber in the likeness of a friend.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena reproaches the princess for leaving fine clothes unwashed before marriage.

segs.speaker: Nausicaa
segs.caption: Papa dear, will you not have the high wagon yoked for me, so I can take our fine clothes to the river and wash them? You yourself need clean linen for the council, and five sons in this house are forever wanting fresh things for the dancing.

segs.speaker: Alcinous
segs.caption: Neither mules nor anything else do I grudge you, child. Go — the servants will yoke the high wagon, the one with the box for the wash.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Her mother packs food, wine, and oil.

items.title: Laundry and Ball at the River

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Nausicaa and her maids drive to the washing pools, unharness the mules, and tread the clothes clean.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Nausicaa spread garments on the shore, bathe, eat, and play ball while the clothes dry.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena deflects the ball into deep water.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The girls cry out.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The shout wakes Odysseus beneath the leaves.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus debates whether to clasp Nausicaa's knees or speak from a distance.

segs.speaker: Nausicaa
segs.caption: Stranger, you seem neither base nor witless, and Zeus deals fortune as he wills — what he gives, a man must bear. But you have come to our land now, and you shall lack neither clothing nor anything owed a hard-tried suppliant. Stand, girls — this man is no enemy; wash him where the river gives shelter, and set food and oil beside him.

items.title: Athena Hides the Walk through Scheria

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Nausicaa reaches the palace while Odysseus waits in Athena's grove.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Nausicaa enters the city wrapped in a divine mist.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena appears as a young girl carrying a pitcher and guides him through streets and harbor.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: These Phaeacians love oar and sail and do not warm to strangers, so walk quickly and question no one. Go straight through the hall to the queen, Arete, whom the people honor like a god. Win her heart, and you may yet see your home and your own high-roofed house.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus stops before Alcinous's palace, dazzled by bronze walls, golden doors, and guardian dogs.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus observes the fifty women weaving and grinding within.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus crosses the threshold under mist and finds the royal feast in progress.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena's mist falls away only when Odysseus reaches Arete.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Arete, daughter of Rhexenor, after many trials I come to your knees, and to your king, and to all these feasters — may the gods give you long joy. For me, ask only this: grant me convoy to my own country, for I have suffered long, far from everyone I love.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus is seated beside the king, fed, and promised a convoy home.

touch.text: Clasp the queen's knees: close your hand

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: How you obtained them?

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Hard to tell all my griefs, queen, for the gods have given me many. Far off lies an island where the goddess Calypso held me seven years against my will, and when at last I sailed, the sea broke my raft and threw me naked on your shore. It was your daughter who found me, fed me, and gave me these clothes — blame her for nothing, for I chose to walk behind alone, fearing men's idle talk.

segs.speaker: Alcinous
segs.caption: One thing only my daughter missed, that she did not bring you straight to our doors — yet your care does you credit, stranger. Would to Zeus a man like you might stay, and be called my son, with house and wealth from my hand. But no one holds you against your will: tomorrow you shall have ship and oarsmen for your home, though it lie farther than the farthest island.

books.title: A Day for Songs and Contests

items.title: The Phaeacian Assembly and the Ship

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: At dawn Athena moves through the city in a herald's form, calling the people to assembly.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena makes Odysseus appear larger and more impressive as he enters.

segs.speaker: Alcinous
segs.caption: Draw a black ship down to the bright sea, and let fifty-two picked youths make her ready for the voyage. The rest of you, lords, come to my hall — we feast this stranger. And summon Demodocus, for to him the god has given song beyond all others.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The people ready the vessel while the palace fills for celebration.

items.title: The Trojan Horse Song and the Name

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Sing now: the Greeks' emergence, the sack, and Odysseus's attack on Deiphobus's house.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus weeps like a captive woman over a fallen husband.

segs.speaker: Alcinous
segs.caption: Stop the lyre, Demodocus — not all here take joy of it, for since the song began our guest has not once left off weeping. Now, stranger, hide it no longer: tell me the name your father and mother called you, and your land and your city. And say why you weep at the doom of the Argives and Troy — did some kinsman fall there, or a comrade dear as a brother?

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus prepares to narrate his wanderings.

touch.text: Hand Demodocus the lyre: pinch it

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Alcinous, mighty king, it is a fine thing to hear a singer such as this, whose voice is like a god's. No moment is sweeter than when joy holds a whole people — feasters ranged down the hall listening, the tables full of bread and meat, the steward pouring wine. This seems to my own heart the fairest thing there is.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: But you ask my name, and I will hide it no longer. I am Odysseus, son of Laertes, known to all men for my cunning, and my fame goes up to heaven.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus describes Ithaca's rugged beauty and his longing to return.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus begins the account of the disasters that followed Troy.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus's fleet sacks Ismarus and divides the captured wealth.

segs.speaker: Odysseus's fleet crews
segs.caption: Not yet, captain! The sheep are fat and the wine runs dark and sweet — one more cup on the beach, and then we row!

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Cicones from inland arrive in organized force and fight through the day.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Six men from every ship are killed before the fleet escapes at dusk.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: A north wind drives the ships off course for nine days.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: They land among the Lotus-eaters and send three scouts inland.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The inhabitants offer lotus.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Those who taste it lose all desire for home.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Take them, though they weep — bind them under the benches! The rest of you aboard and to your oars now, before another man tastes the lotus and forgets his home.

items.title: Goat Island and the Cyclops Coast

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The fleet reaches a fertile unworked island opposite the Cyclopes' land.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: In darkness the ships enter a sheltered harbor and rest.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus takes one ship and selects twelve men to investigate the neighboring people.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus carries a skin of Maron's powerful wine and leads twelve men to a huge cave.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus find cheeses, pails, whey, lambs, and kids arranged by age.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: By whatever you hold sacred, hear me: to steal food and animals and escape.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: No — we wait. I would see the master of this cave myself, and take the guest-gift that strangers are owed. My men saw truer than I, and how much better it would have been to listen.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: At dusk Polyphemus returns carrying a massive load of wood and drives his flock inside.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Polyphemus lifts a stone slab that no ordinary team could move and blocks the entrance.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Polyphemus milks ewes and goats, sets young beneath mothers, curdles milk, and lights a fire.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The hidden men and the giant demands their identity.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: We are Achaeans out of Troy, men of Agamemnon, whose fame is the widest now under heaven — driven here by every wind on the wrong sea-roads. We come to your knees, hoping the welcome due a guest. Respect the gods, mighty one: Zeus himself walks with strangers and avenges them.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus lies that Poseidon smashed it against the rocks.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The Cyclops seizes two men, smashes them on the floor, and devours them raw.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus drinks milk and sleeps among his animals while the survivors pray in horror.

covers.title: The Name Nobody and the Stake

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus considers killing the sleeping giant but realizes the entrance stone would trap them forever.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: At dawn Polyphemus eats two more men and leaves with the flock, sealing the cave again.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus selects a green olive trunk, cuts and smooths it into a stake, and hardens its point in the fire.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The men hide the stake beneath dung and draw lots for four helpers.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Here, Cyclops — drink wine on that man-flesh you have eaten, and learn what drink our ship carried. You ask my name, and I will tell it for the guest-gift you promised: Nobody is my name. Nobody — so my father and mother and all my friends call me.

segs.speaker: Polyphemus
segs.caption: Give me more, freely — and here is your gift, Nobody, to warm your heart: I eat Nobody last, after all his friends. There is my guest-gift to you.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus heats the stake until it glows and the chosen men drive it into the Cyclops's eye.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus twist it as blood and steam erupt.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Polyphemus wakes with a roar and tears it free.

segs.speaker: Cyclopes outside
segs.caption: What ails you, Polyphemus, that you wake the deathless night with screaming — is some man stealing your flocks, or killing you by craft or force? If Nobody harms you, alone as you are, it is sickness sent by Zeus, and cannot be helped — pray to your father Poseidon.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Polyphemus gropes at the entrance while the men hide among the animals.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: At dawn Polyphemus opens the cave and feels every animal's back as it passes.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus binds three rams abreast for each man, suspending a sailor beneath the middle animal.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: I took the great lead ram myself and hung beneath his belly, my hands twisted in that miracle of wool, and dared not breathe. Over my head the blind master mourned to him: Sweet ram, why last from the cave today, you who were always first — do you grieve for your master's eye?

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Outside, the men release themselves, drive the flock to the ship, and row away.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus divide the animals and sacrifice the great ram to Zeus.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Cyclops! It was no weak man's friends you ate in your hollow cave — your evil deeds were bound to find you out! You dared devour guests in your own house, and Zeus and the gods have paid you for it!

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Polyphemus tears off a mountain peak and hurls it, driving a wave that nearly beaches the ship again.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Cyclops — if any mortal ever asks who put out your eye so shamefully, tell him this: it was Odysseus, sacker of cities, who blinded you — Laertes's son, whose home is in Ithaca!

segs.speaker: Polyphemus
segs.caption: So the old prophecy comes home — Telemus foretold I would lose my sight at the hands of Odysseus, and I watched all these years for a great man, not this little worthless nothing who undid me with wine. Hear me, Poseidon, dark-haired shaker of the earth, if I am truly your son: grant that Odysseus, sacker of cities, never reach his home. Or if he must, let him come late and broken, on a stranger's ship, all his comrades lost — and find trouble waiting in his house.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: A second rock misses as the ship escapes to the fleet.

covers.title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds

segs.speaker: Aeolus
segs.caption: Take this bag of oxhide, Odysseus — every rough wind is bound inside, sewn shut with silver wire. I loose the West Wind only; let it carry you home to Ithaca.

segs.speaker: Aeolus
segs.caption: Out of my island — out, worst of living men! You come back cursed; the blessed gods themselves hate you. I give no help to what heaven hunts.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The fleet enters a narrow harbor ringed by cliffs.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus alone moors outside.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Your parents' house.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The queen summons Antiphates, who seizes and eats one scout.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus cuts his cable and escapes with only his own ship.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The lone ship reaches Aeaea and the exhausted survivors rest for two days.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus climbs a lookout and sees smoke inland, then kills a great stag for food.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus divides the crew into two groups and draws lots.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurylochus leads twenty-two men toward Circe's house while Odysseus remains with the ship.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The scouts find Circe singing at her loom while enchanted wolves and lions fawn around them.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: All but Eurylochus enter.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Circe serves drugged food and strikes them with her wand.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The men become pigs in body while retaining human minds.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Circe shuts them in pens and throws them acorns.

segs.speaker: Eurylochus
segs.caption: They are gone, Odysseus — all of them! They went in at the shining doors and not one came out. I waited long, and called, and no man answered.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus arms himself and heads alone toward Circe's house despite Eurylochus's protest.

segs.speaker: Hermes
segs.caption: Where now, unlucky man, alone through these hills and knowing nothing of the ground? Your friends are penned as pigs in Circe's sties — and you march straight in to join them.

segs.speaker: Hermes
segs.caption: Here — take this herb of power and carry it against her drugs. The gods call it moly: black at the root, its flower white as milk. Hard for mortal men to dig, but the gods can do all things.

segs.speaker: Hermes
segs.caption: When she strikes you with her wand, draw your sword and rush her as if to kill. And before you go to her bed, make her swear the great oath of the gods that she plots no further harm — lest she strip you naked and unman you.

touch.text: Take the moly from Hermes: pinch it

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Circe serves Odysseus the drugged mixture and strikes him with her wand.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The moly protects him.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: he draws his sword and rushes her.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Circe recognizes the foretold man, kneels, and offers her bed.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus requires the binding oath that she will not unman or harm him.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: No. I will not eat while his crew remain imprisoned.

items.text: The men restored, and a year of feasting in Circe's hall, until they want home.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Circe, keep now the promise that you made me: send me home. My own heart strains for Ithaca, and my men's hearts with mine — will you loose us at last?

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: To the house of Death? Before Ithaca I must sail down to Hades and question blind Tiresias of Thebes? Then that is the road, though it breaks every heart aboard.

segs.speaker: Circe
segs.caption: Set your mast and sit still — the North Wind will carry you across Ocean to Persephone's grove of poplar and willow. There dig a trench a cubit square, and pour to all the dead honey and milk, sweet wine, water, and white barley. Bleed a ram and a black ewe into it — the dead will come, but hold them from the blood until Tiresias has drunk.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Elpenor, sleeping on the roof, wakes confused, falls, and dies unnoticed.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The crew launches in grief while Circe sends a favorable wind.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The ship reaches the misty land of the Cimmerians at Ocean's edge.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus digs a trench, pours libations, sacrifices sheep, and holds the spirits back with his sword.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The dead gather in multitudes, crying around the blood.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus waits for Tiresias before allowing any other shade to drink.

touch.text: Hold the shades back: point at the pit and hold

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Elpenor's unburied ghost approaches first and Odysseus weeps in recognition.

segs.speaker: Elpenor's shade
segs.caption: Burn me with all my armor and heap a mound by the grey sea, for an unlucky man that men to come may know of. And plant above it the oar I pulled while I lived among my friends — will you do this for me?

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: All this I will do, poor Elpenor — I will leave nothing undone. When I stand again on Aeaea, fire and mound and oar shall be yours.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Tiresias drinks the blood and recognizes Odysseus.

segs.speaker: Tiresias
segs.caption: You seek a honey-sweet homecoming, but a god will make it bitter. The Earthshaker holds his grudge — you blinded the son he loved, and he does not forget.

segs.speaker: Tiresias
segs.caption: Hear me, all of you: when you come to Thrinacia, where the cattle of the Sun graze, keep your hands from those herds. Harm them, and I foretell ruin for ship and crew — and if you yourself escape, you come home late and wretched, on a stranger's ship, with every companion lost.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Tiresias foretells Odysseus's lone return, the suitors' punishment, and a final inland journey carrying an oar.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: After a distant sacrifice to Poseidon, death will come gently in old age.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Come, mother — drink of the blood and know me. It is I, alive, your son.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus describes Penelope's fidelity, Telemachus's position, and Laertes's isolated grief.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: No sickness took you, then. It was longing — longing for me, for my counsels and my gentleness — that stole the honey of your life. My going killed you, mother.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus tries three times to embrace her, but his arms pass through the shade.

items.text: The shades of queens and of Agamemnon crowd to the blood.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Achilles approaches with Patroclus, Antilochus, and Ajax nearby.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Achilles, no man was ever more blessed, nor will be: alive we honored you like a god, and here you rule with power among the dead. Do not grieve at dying — you of all men.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Would you hear of Peleus, and of your son Neoptolemus? Of your father I know nothing — but of the boy I can speak truly, for I myself brought him from Scyros to the war.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Achilles strides away rejoicing.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: No. I will not reconciliation and withdraws in silence.

items.text: The dead come on in thousands and he runs for the ship. On Aeaea they bury Elpenor, and Circe draws the way ahead: the Sirens, Scylla and Charybdis, the island of the Sun.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The wind dies as the ship approaches the Sirens' island.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus softens wax and seals every crewman's ears.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The men bind him upright to the mast and row past the flowered shore.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The Sirens promise total knowledge.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus struggles and signals to be released.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Perimedes and Eurylochus tighten the ropes until the song fades.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The crew hears Charybdis roar and sees spray rising from the whirlpool.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Row, friends — we have been in worse and lived, and this too we shall remember. Helmsman, hold her off that smoke and hug the cliff — keep to the rock, or you kill us all.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus arms himself despite Circe's warning and searches the rock face.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Scylla's six heads strike, lifting six screaming men from the ship.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The survivors pass beyond both monsters while watching their companions die above them.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The exhausted crew sees the cattle and sheep of Helios on Thrinacia.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Row on — we do not land here. Tiresias and Circe both warned me alike: our worst harm waits on that island. Call me merciless if you will, Eurylochus — I would keep you alive.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The men swear to touch no livestock and land for one night.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: A month of storm winds traps them while stores diminish.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus repeatedly reminds them of the oath.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurylochus persuades the crew to sacrifice the best cattle rather than starve.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurylochus substitute oak leaves for barley and water for wine, kill the animals, and roast the meat.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The hides crawl and the meat bellows on the spits.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Lampetie tells Helios, who demands punishment from Zeus.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: What have you done — you have slaughtered the Sun's own herds while I slept! O father Zeus, you lulled me to my ruin. This is doom, and no offering on earth will unmake it.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: On the seventh day the wind falls and the ship leaves Thrinacia.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Zeus gathers a black cloud and strikes the mast with lightning.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The ship shatters and every crewman drowns.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus lashes keel and mast together.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Driven back to Charybdis, he hangs from the fig tree until the timbers reemerge, then drifts alone to Calypso.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus finishes his tale and the Phaeacians sit in silence.

segs.speaker: Alcinous
segs.caption: Bring out one more chest, and let every lord of Phaeacia add a tripod and a cauldron to it. Then set the feast, for our guest sails at sundown and he must leave us glad.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: At sunset Odysseus boards the convoy ship and lies on a prepared bed in the stern.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The crew carries the sleeping man and his treasure onto the shore.

items.title: Odysseus Wakes on an Unknown Shore

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: What land is this now, and what people? The very air is a stranger to me.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Tripods, cauldrons, the woven robes, the gold. All of it here, nothing taken. Then why does this shore know nothing of me, unless those sailors dumped me on some foreign coast?

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Wretched again, and among strangers again. O Zeus, where do I carry all this wealth, and where do I carry myself?

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Good day to you, stranger. You look like a man who has lost his road.

items.title: The Cretan Lie Meets Its Match

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The shepherd tells Odysseus you is in Ithaca and the hero suppresses your joy.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Cunning, insatiable trickster, even in your own land you will not lay your lies aside! Enough now: I am Athena, daughter of Zeus, and we two are alike, crooked-minded both, you the best of mortals at scheming and I of gods.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Hard goddess, where were you all the salt years since Troy burned? You stood at my shoulder then, and after, I never once saw you on my deck while I suffered. Now you come smiling and tell me this is Ithaca, so swear it is not one more mockery.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: So that is the shape of it. Poseidon's wrath made open rescue too costly, and you wore silence the way I wear rags. You hid me even from my own eyes to keep me breathing.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena helps Odysseus carry the gifts into the cave of the nymphs.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena seals the cave entrance with a stone and sits with him beneath the olive tree.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena count the suitors and devise a concealment strategy.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Go first to your swineherd Eumaeus, keeper of your pigs and lover of your house, and stay by his fire and question everything. I go to Sparta, to fetch your son home.

touch.text: Seal the treasure cave: push the stone

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena touches Odysseus with her wand and shrivels his skin, hair, and limbs.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Dimmed eyes, wracked limbs, rags fit for burning on an old man's back. No one who ever loved you will look at you twice. Take this staff and this patched beggar's sack, for this is who you are now.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena departs for Sparta and Odysseus walks toward Eumaeus's farm.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus approaches Eumaeus's remote pig farm in disguise.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus runs out, scatters the dogs with stones, and brings the stranger inside.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus offers his own seat and prepares two young pigs for a meal.

touch.text: Calm the dogs: show an open palm

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus apologizes for the humble food and curses the suitors who consume Odysseus's best animals.

segs.speaker: Eumaeus
segs.caption: My master, and I will say his name, Odysseus, was kind to me past any telling, and the sea has him now, dead in some far water. Every drifter who wants supper sings me a tale that he lives. I have stopped believing songs.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Then hear an oath, not a song. By Zeus of guests, by this table and this fire: Odysseus comes home before this year is out. When he stands in his own hall, give me a cloak and tunic then, and not one hour before.

segs.speaker: Eumaeus
segs.caption: Keep your oath, friend, for I'll pay no cloak on it, and Odysseus will not come. Drink your wine and speak of other things; my heart aches enough whenever his name is said.

books.title: The Prince Sets Sail for Home

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Telemachus, wake. It is wrong to wander while your house is eaten hollow. Go home now, before your mother's own kin bend her to marry Eurymachus and your inheritance walks out the door with her.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: When you touch Ithaca, send ship and crew round to the town without you. Go first, on foot, to the swineherd Eumaeus, who keeps faith with your house; sleep there, and send him to tell your mother you are safely home.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus wakes Pisistratus and prepares to depart at dawn.

items.text: Gifts at Sparta; the ship runs home past the ambush.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Theoclymenus reads the omen as proof that Odysseus's line will remain supreme.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Crew, take her round to the town harbor without me; I go inland to look over my farms. Tonight I lodge with the herdsmen, and tomorrow evening I'll set out a feast to pay you for the voyage.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus entrusts Theoclymenus to Piraeus and walks inland alone.

touch.text: Row ashore in secret: pump your hand

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus approaches Eumaeus's farm and the dogs greet him without aggression.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus recognizes him, drops his bowl, and kisses him like a father receiving a lost son.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The disguised Odysseus rises and offers his seat.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Keep your seat, stranger. Eumaeus will pile me brushwood. Tell me instead who you are, and what ship set you down on Ithaca.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena restores Odysseus's strength, clothing, skin, and dark hair outside the hut.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena reenters transformed.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus recoils, believing he is a god.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: I am no god. Why do you liken me to the immortals? I am your father, Telemachus, the man you have grieved for all these years.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: You are not my father. No mortal man makes himself young at will, and no beggar puts on a king in one breath. This is a god's work, and it is mocking my grief.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus embrace and weep with the force of birds robbed of their young.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: The Phaeacians rowed me home asleep and left me with their gifts on the shore. Now tell me plainly: how many suitors, and out of what houses?

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Fifty-two from Dulichium, twenty-four from Same, twenty from Zacynthus, twelve of Ithaca itself, with a herald and a singer beside them. A hundred and eight, Father, and we are two. Two men cannot stand against so many in that hall.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Zeus and Athena stand with us, and they are worth more than a hundred spears. Carry every weapon out of the hall to the storeroom, and leave two swords, two spears, two shields where our hands can reach them.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus must return to the palace, endure insults, and tell no one, not even Penelope or Laertes.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus assign Eumaeus to bring the beggar later.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena changes Odysseus back into the old beggar before Eumaeus returns.

segs.speaker: Eumaeus
segs.caption: The prince is home and safe, and I put the word in the queen's ear myself. The ship that lay in wait for him came slinking into harbor with empty hands.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The three men eat and sleep while father and son preserve the secret.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus leads the disguised Odysseus from the farm toward town.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Look at this. One filthy tramp leading another down to beg at better men's tables. Out of my road, before my foot teaches you where the door is.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus suppresses the urge to kill him and continues toward the palace.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Near the palace Odysseus sees his old dog Argos lying neglected on dung.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus turns aside to hide a tear while asking Eumaeus about the animal.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: After twenty years Argos dies as soon as he has recognized Odysseus.

touch.text: Stroke old Argos: move your hand gently side to side

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus enters first and Telemachus signals him to seat the beggar at the door.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus crosses his own threshold unrecognized and hears Phemius singing.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Give what you can spare, my lord. You have plenty and it costs you nothing. I was a rich man once with a house of my own, and I fed every wanderer who came to my door.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Most give food while Antinous demands to know who admitted him.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: I had a house and men of my own once, and I gave to any beggar who came. Then Egypt swallowed it. My crew were cut down along the river and I was sold from hand to hand until I came to this door.

segs.speaker: Antinous
segs.caption: What god dumped this plague on our dinner? Back from the table, you shameless thing, before you find an Egypt worse than the first.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Antinous hurls a footstool into his shoulder.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Hear me, gods, and you avengers of the poor, if a beggar has any claim on heaven. Let Antinous meet his death before his wedding day.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Even the other suitors condemn the violation of a stranger.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Look, then. The rags come up, and you may all see what the sea left me.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena enlarges his appearance.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Irus trembles but is forced into the ring.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus chooses not to kill him and breaks his jaw with one compact blow.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Sit there in the dirt and keep the dogs and the pigs off yourself. You were king of the beggars an hour ago. Come back to this gate and you will not walk away from it.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Cheer and Amphinomus gives the victor food and wine.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena places a desire in Penelope to appear before the suitors and inflame their gifts.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena puts the queen to sleep, beautifies her, and wakes her radiant.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Penelope descends with two maids and rebukes Telemachus for allowing the stranger's abuse.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: When Odysseus left me he took my wrist and said, when the boy's beard shows, marry whom you will. That day has come. But what suitors are you, who eat another man's cattle and bring the bride nothing?

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The suitors send for jewels, robes, and ornaments while Odysseus silently rejoices at her strategy.

items.text: Evening in the hall: the suitors drink; the maids mock the beggar at the fire.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Every spear and every shield goes out of this hall tonight, and quietly. If they ask, the smoke has eaten them. The iron itself draws a man on.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena carries a golden lamp while father and son take shields, spears, and helmets to the storeroom.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Nurse, keep the women shut in their rooms until this is done. The smoke has ruined the bronze my father left. And when men are deep in wine I will not have a blade within reach of a quarrel.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The hall is left apparently defenseless for the future contest.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus invents the Cretan name Aethon and claims to have hosted Odysseus before Troy.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus describes the king's purple cloak, golden brooch, tunic, and herald Eurybates in exact detail.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Penelope weeps as if melting snow while Odysseus keeps his eyes hard despite inward grief.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Stranger, you were pitied in this house an hour ago. Now you will be loved in it and honored. Those were my gifts, folded by me, and no living man could have known them who had not stood beside him.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: You swear to me he is near, and comes before this moon is dead. Then hear my own oath, stranger. If he crosses that threshold, no one alive will ever call you beggar again.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Eurycleia, rise and wash the feet of your master's age-mate. By now the hands and feet of Odysseus must be worn as this man's are, if he is still under the sun.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus recognizes the danger but cannot refuse without suspicion.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus drops the foot into the basin, spilling water, and reaches toward Penelope.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus grips her throat gently but firmly and makes her swear silence.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: At dawn he hunts with his uncles on Mount Parnassus.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: A boar bursts from dense cover and charges.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus spears it but receives a deep tusk wound above the knee.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The hunters bind the wound, stop the blood with a charm, and carry him home.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Hear my dream, stranger, and tell me what it means. Twenty geese feed at my trough and I love to watch them. Then a great eagle stoops from the mountain and breaks the neck of every one.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: There is no second reading of it, lady. The dream has told you its own meaning, and it has named the day of their death.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Tomorrow I will set out the great bow of Odysseus and the twelve axes he used to line up and shoot an arrow through. Whoever strings that bow and sends the shaft clean through them all, that man I will follow. And I will leave this house that I loved.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Dreams come through two gates, stranger: one of horn that comes true, one of ivory that lies to us. I think mine came the wrong way. Good night to you.

items.text: A sleepless night; at dawn, thunder out of a clear sky.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurycleia wakes the household and servants prepare the hall for Apollo's feast day.

segs.speaker: Eumaeus
segs.caption: Good morning, stranger. Do the men treat you any better today, or is the house still the house it was?

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Melanthius enters with goats and renews his abuse.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Philoetius brings cattle, takes the stranger's hand, and weeps because he resembles Odysseus.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Herdsman, mark what I say, and let the gods hear it. Before you drive your cattle home again, Odysseus will stand in this house, and you will see with your own eyes the suitors killed.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena drives the suitors into uncontrollable laughter while their meat drips blood in their vision.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Theoclymenus sees darkness covering them, ghosts crowding the court, and blood on the walls.

segs.speaker: Theoclymenus
segs.caption: Your heads are wrapped in darkness and your knees are gone. The walls are running with blood, the porch is full of ghosts going down to the dark, and the sun has died out of the sky. Laugh. I am going out of this house while its door still opens.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus and Odysseus watch one another across the doomed feast.

touch.text: Shield your eyes from the vision: open palm

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena inspires Penelope to begin the contest that will expose the suitors to slaughter.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The queen enters the storeroom, unlocks the doors, and lifts Odysseus's bow and quiver down.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena sits with the weapon across her knees and weeps before carrying it to the hall.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Two maids bring the chest of axes and set the implements before the suitors.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Hear me, lords. Here is the great bow of Odysseus. Whoever strings it with his own hands and sends an arrow clean through all twelve axes, I will go with that man, and leave this house I came to as a bride.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus and Philoetius weep at the sight of their master's weapon.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Antinous rebukes them.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus plants the axes in a straight line and tries the bow three times.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: On the fourth attempt he nearly strings it, but Odysseus signals him to stop.

segs.speaker: Leiodes
segs.caption: I cannot bend it. Let another try. But I tell you, this bow will take the life and the breath out of the best men here, and better to die than live on failing at what we came for.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: One after another the men strain, sweat, and fail.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Melanthius lights a fire and brings fat so the bow can be warmed and greased.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Even Eurymachus cannot string it and suffers humiliation.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Antinous postpones the contest for Apollo's festival feast.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus follows Eumaeus and Philoetius outside and tests their loyalty.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Then look. Here is the scar the boar gave me on Parnassus. I am Odysseus. I am home, in the twentieth year, and I stand in front of you.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The herdsmen embrace him and weep, then swear support.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: No more tears. Eumaeus, when they shout you down, carry the bow to me anyway and put it in my hands. Philoetius, bar the courtyard gate and lash it fast. And tell Eurycleia to lock the women in their rooms and let no one out, whatever they hear.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Hear me, lords. Let me put my hands on the bow, only to learn whether any strength is left in these arms, or whether the road has eaten it all.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The suitors erupt in anger and fear that a beggar may succeed.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Let the stranger have the bow. He is a guest in my house, and no guest is refused here. And if he strings it, I will give him a cloak and a tunic, a spear, and a sword, and send him wherever his heart wants to go.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: Mother, the bow is mine to give, and no man in Ithaca will overrule me in my own house. Go up to your room and your loom. The talking here belongs to the men.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eumaeus carries the bow through the shouting crowd to Odysseus.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurycleia locks the women into their quarters at Telemachus's instruction.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Philoetius fastens the courtyard gate with a ship's cable.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus turns the bow in his hands, inspecting every part while the suitors mock him.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The hidden allies take their assigned positions and the escape routes close.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus strings the bow effortlessly, as a musician strings a lyre.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Hear that. It still sings.

segs.speaker: Zeus
segs.caption: It is time, son of Laertes. I have set my sign on the day.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus places sword and spear beside him and moves to his father's side.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus nocks an arrow and shoots cleanly through all twelve axes.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Telemachus, the stranger sitting in your hall has not disgraced you. I did not miss the mark, and the bow did not wear me out. Now it is the hour for supper, while there is still light, and after supper there is other sport in this house.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus strips off his rags, leaps onto the threshold, and pours the remaining arrows before him.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus shoots Antinous through the throat while the suitor lifts a cup.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Antinous falls across the table, spilling food and wine as the room erupts.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The suitors assume an accident and search for weapons that are no longer there.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: You dogs. You never thought I would come home from Troy. You ate my house, you forced my women, you courted my wife while I still lived.

touch.text: Loose the arrow: pinch and open

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurymachus blames Antinous and offers repayment many times over if Odysseus spares them.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Eurymachus, if you gave me all your fathers' wealth, my hands would not stop. Fight or run. Not one of you goes out of this door alive.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurymachus rallies the suitors to rush the archer beneath raised tables.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus shoots Eurymachus in the chest.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Amphinomus charges and Telemachus kills him with a spear.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus runs to the storeroom and brings shields, helmets, and spears for Odysseus, Eumaeus, Philoetius, and himself.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus admits leaving the door unbarred after one trip.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The defenders arm in formation while Odysseus continues firing.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: When the arrows run low they transition to spear combat.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Melanthius discovers the open storeroom route and carries weapons to the suitors.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Eumaeus, Philoetius. Someone is arming them out of my own storeroom. Go up, find him, and bring me his hands tied behind his back.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus catch Melanthius returning for more arms.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus bind his hands and feet, hoist him by a rope to the rafters, and leave him suspended in pain.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena enters in Mentor's form.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Mentor, keep ruin off me. Remember the friend who honored you all his life. Or have you come late on purpose, now the work is nearly done?

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus rebukes him but first tests his strength by remaining disguised and partially withholding help.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The suitors throw spears.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena deflects them into walls and doors.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The defenders answer with a coordinated volley and kill several men.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena raises her aegis from the roof beam and terror breaks the remaining formation.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus and his allies pursue the suitors through the hall like falcons among smaller birds.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Leiodes clasps Odysseus's knees but is killed despite claiming innocence.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Phemius and Medon appeal for mercy and Telemachus confirms their limited complicity.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Live, both of you. My son has spoken for you. Go out to the courtyard and sit by the altar until this work is finished.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The living search the blood-filled hall for any remaining threat.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Rejoice in your heart, old woman, but not aloud. It is not holy to crow over dead men. Bring me fire and sulphur now, and I will cleanse this hall.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Loyal women enter, recognize him, and embrace him in tears.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus receives them while restraining grief and maintaining security.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus sends Eurycleia upstairs to wake Penelope and announce that her husband has returned.

segs.speaker: Eurycleia
segs.caption: Wake, my child, wake and see it with your own eyes. Odysseus is home, here in this house, and every suitor lies dead in the hall. The man you have mourned twenty years is sitting by his own fire.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Penelope first thinks the nurse has gone mad or that a god punished the men.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Eurycleia offers the scar as proof and describes the king waiting below.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Penelope descends, divided between embracing him and testing him from a distance.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Telemachus rebukes her for hardness.

segs.speaker: Telemachus
segs.caption: She will not come near you, father. She says the two of you keep signs no other soul has ever heard. Until those signs are spoken, she says, I am no son of hers to argue it.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Let her take her time; my wife will know me in her own hour. There is a colder danger at the door. Kill one man in this land and his kinsmen come armed, and we have killed the flower of Ithaca.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Wash yourselves and put on fresh tunics; let the singer strike up a wedding tune. Let every man who passes this gate say the queen has married at last. No word of the dead leaves this house until I give it.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus bathes while Athena restores his stature and beauty.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Phemius plays the lyre and the household dances so neighbors believe a wedding is underway.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: Strange woman. The gods have given you a heart that nothing softens. Then let it stand; nurse, make up a bed for me alone, and I will sleep apart in my own house.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: No other wife would sit across the room from a husband home in the twentieth year, worn down by salt and war. Your heart is harder than the stone under this floor.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Eurycleia, carry the great bed out of the bridal chamber and set it up in the hall. Spread the fleeces and the bright blankets on it for him there.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus erupts, explaining that he built the bed around a living olive tree and no one could move it intact.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The secret proves identity.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Penelope runs to him and embraces him.

segs.speaker: Penelope
segs.caption: Do not be angry with me; of all men you were always the shrewdest. I was afraid some stranger would come with a smooth story and take me with it. Now the sign has come and my heart gives way, and you are as welcome to me as dry land to swimmers.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Athena holds back dawn while husband and wife weep and reunite.

items.text: Athena holds back the dawn. In the morning he walks out to his father's farm.

items.title: The Scar and the Orchard Trees

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus shows the boar scar as physical proof.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: And count the trees you gave me when I was a boy trailing you down these rows. Thirteen pear, ten apple, forty fig, and fifty rows of vines, each ripening in its own season. I begged them off you and you named them to me one by one.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Laertes recognizes the private map of inheritance and collapses into his son's arms.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Laertes fears that Ithaca lacks men willing to defend them from the suitors' kin.

segs.speaker: Athena
segs.caption: Hold, men of Ithaca! Break off this bitter war, and part before more blood is spilled.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Zeus hurls a thunderbolt before her feet, making the command irresistible.

segs.speaker: Odysseus
segs.caption: They break and run, and everything in me stoops after them like an eagle. But that was the bolt of Zeus at your feet, and I will not argue with it. I hold.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: Odysseus establishes binding oaths between king and people in Mentor's form.

segs.speaker: Epic Narrator
segs.caption: The poem ends with the household restored and the violence converted into civic peace.

touch.text: Make peace: show an open palm
